classification.difficultyReason: Read each marked length as radius or diameter and apply the taught sphere or hemisphere formulas, including the flat circular face for hemisphere total area. Repeated parts and fractional values add no new conceptual demand.

content.prompt: Find the volume and total surface area of each of the spheres and hemispheres shown below:

spec.description: Unfilled sphere with equatorial ellipse and centre-to-right radius.
Unfilled sphere with equatorial ellipse and centre-to-right radius.
Unfilled sphere with equatorial ellipse and full horizontal diameter.
Unfilled sphere with equatorial ellipse and full horizontal diameter.
Unfilled hemisphere with elliptical base and centre-to-right base radius.
spec.mathematics: Radius 4 m; total surface includes the circular base.

answer.worked:
The total surface area includes the circular base.

$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi(4)^3\\V&=\frac{128\pi}{3}\,\mathrm{m}^{3}\\A&=2\pi(4)^2+\pi(4)^2\\A&=48\pi\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled hemisphere with elliptical base and centre-to-right base radius.
spec.mathematics: Radius 2/3 m; total surface includes the circular base.

answer.worked:
The total surface area includes the circular base.

$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3\\V&=\frac{16\pi}{81}\,\mathrm{m}^{3}\\A&=2\pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2+\pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2\\A&=\frac{4\pi}{3}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled hemisphere with elliptical base and full horizontal base diameter.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 6 m; total surface includes the circular base.

answer.worked:
The total surface area includes the circular base.

$$\begin{align*}r&=6\div2=3\,\mathrm{m}\\V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi(3)^3\\V&=18\pi\,\mathrm{m}^{3}\\A&=2\pi(3)^2+\pi(3)^2\\A&=27\pi\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled hemisphere with elliptical base and full horizontal base diameter.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 1/3 cm; total surface includes the circular base.

answer.worked:
The total surface area includes the circular base.

$$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{1}{3}\div2=\frac{1}{6}\,\mathrm{cm}\\V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^3\\V&=\frac{\pi}{324}\,\mathrm{cm}^{3}\\A&=2\pi\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^2+\pi\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^2\\A&=\frac{\pi}{12}\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
